what: General Mills makes packaged food. Cheerios, Nature Valley, Betty Crocker, Pillsbury, Yoplait in some markets, Häagen-Dazs internationally, and Blue Buffalo pet food are among its brands.
customers: Supermarket and club store shoppers in North America and internationally, plus pet owners and foodservice customers.
money: cereal, snacks, baking and meals sold through grocers
food sold to restaurants and institutions
Häagen-Dazs and other brands outside North America
moat: Brands with decades of shelf presence and household habit, plus manufacturing and distribution scale that private label competitors partly match but national rivals do not.
risks: It reported a loss after writing down the value of brands
Revenue has fallen about 3% a year over three years as volumes decline
Consumers have shifted to cheaper own-brand products
Debt of about $13 billion against almost no cash
opportunities: Pet food grows faster than packaged food and is more defensible
Gross margin of 34% leaves room for cost reduction
watch: Organic volume trends and pet segment growth.
